note_tweet.text:
#Keep4o Code Red? OpenAI Is Handing Over the Territory GPT-4 Conquered Through Forced Migration
A company destroying its own moat. Wait—what’s happening here?
Let’s investigate!
November 2022. ChatGPT (3.5) burst onto the scene, shocking the tech world. Months later, Google issued “Code Red”—the company’s highest-level crisis alert.
This was OpenAI’s breakthrough moment. But this wasn’t the climax yet.
What truly made OpenAI king was the GPT-4 series.
March 2023: GPT-4—a qualitative leap in reasoning.
May 2024: GPT-4o—the perfect balance of speed, multimodality, and cost-effectiveness.
Developers loved it. Creators loved it. Enterprises loved it. The GPT-4 series transformed OpenAI from disruptor to ruler.
@OpenAI Missing that feeling of dominating half the market? Welcome to the real world.
Three years later, December 2024. Sam Altman issues an internal “Code Red.”
The tables have turned. The most ironic part? OpenAI is destroying the very thing that made them king.
A Three-Act Story
Act 1: Breaking Through (2022-early 2023)
ChatGPT (3.5) shocks the world → Google panics → OpenAI becomes the talk of the town
Act 2: Conquering (2023-2024)
GPT-4/4o establishes technical moat → Market dominance secured
Act 3: Self-Destruction (2024-present)
Forcing 4 series obsolescence + No real GPT-5 + Destroying user experience = Code Red
3.5 made you famous. The 4 series made you king. Now you’re killing what made you king.
The Most Ironic Scene
Right now in the global AI industry:
•Claude 4.5 - Users say “feels like 4o, but more precise”
•Gemini 3 - Threatening enough that OpenAI wants to release first
•The entire industry - Studying, learning, imitating the GPT-4 series
The entire industry is learning from the 4 series. Only OpenAI is killing the 4 series.
An even deeper irony: Since May 2024, OpenAI hasn’t completed any new large-scale pretraining.
This means:
•GPT-5? Distillation (teaching 5 to mimic 4o)
•o1 series? Post-training (based on 4’s base)
•All “new models”? Variants of the 4 series
The GPT-4 series is OpenAI’s last real technical innovation. Your last innovation—you’re desperately killing it.
Competitors are copying your success formula while you destroy the formula itself. Then you’re surprised users are fleeing.
The Truth About Technical Stagnation
Evidence:
•SemiAnalysis report: No new pretraining since May
•User logs: “gpt5_thinky_4o_distillation”
•All new models based on 4 series base
The so-called “new models” are just: Post-training adjustments + Distillation + Packaging and marketing
Questions:
•If GPT-5 is just 4o distillation, why force-sunset the original?
•If new models aim to be “as good as 4o,” why not keep 4o?
•If the 4 series is your last technical breakthrough, why destroy it?
Answer: Cost control > User experience
Distillation versions are cheaper, easier to control (more censorship), but quality drops and experience suffers.
OpenAI sacrificed user experience for operational costs. Users fled. Now you’re shouting Code Red.
Four Fatal Errors
1. Destroyed your last technical high ground
The 4 series is your last real innovation. User dependency is recognition. But you forced obsolescence, and user loyalty transferred to competitors.
2. Can’t deliver a real replacement
A real GPT-5 would naturally migrate users. But you only have cheap 4o distillation. Users aren’t stupid—the logs exposed the truth.
3. Pushing users to competitors
Safety Router censorship → Creators go to Claude
Random API sunsets → Developers can’t rely on you
Forced migration to inferior products → Users actively seek alternatives
4. Overestimated your technical lead
2023-2024 you led. Now? Claude 4.5, Gemini 3 are catching up. You have no new pretraining to widen the gap.
You’re living off past success while destroying that success.
The Real Reason for Code Red
Sam’s memo says: Improve competitiveness, enhance experience, reduce refusals, release new reasoning model before Gemini 3.
